import { Steps, Aside, CardGrid, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import BuildAppPipeline from '../../../components/diagrams/BuildAppPipeline.astro';

This takes core's `apps/kv-store` from source to a method call on a local
cluster, then packs it the way a real cluster installs it. Everything runs from
a checkout of [core](https://github.com/calimero-network/core); the
[tutorial](/build/tutorial/) writes an app of your own and explains each step.

<BuildAppPipeline />

<Aside type="note">
  The commands are `apps/kv-store/`, `crates/merod` and the CLI definitions in
  `crates/meroctl/src`. Run
  `meroctl <command> --help` to check them against your build; every command is
  in the [meroctl reference](/operate/meroctl/).
</Aside>

<Steps>

1. **Install the tools.** Rust with the `wasm32-wasip2` target (core's
   `rust-toolchain.toml` lists it), `meroctl`, and `merod` for the local
   cluster:

   ```sh
   rustup target add wasm32-wasip2
   cargo install --locked --path crates/meroctl
   cargo install --locked --path crates/merod
   ```

2. **Test the app** on the real engine, with no node. The tests build the crate
   into a component and run it with `TestApp` (`calimero-sdk`'s `testing`
   feature):

   ```sh
   cargo test --manifest-path apps/kv-store/Cargo.toml
   ```

3. **Build the component**:

   ```sh
   meroctl app build apps/kv-store --out kv_store.wasm
   ```

   It compiles the crate for `wasm32-wasip2`, makes it a `calimero:app`
   component and lifts the ABI the macros wrote into its `calimero:abi`
   section.

4. **Start a development cluster**: three nodes of `merod local` in the
   background on `127.0.0.1:2501`-`2503`, mock attestation, state in
   `.merod-local/`. `meroctl` saves it as the node `local` (trusting its mock
   quote), the default when you have none:

   ```sh
   meroctl local up
   meroctl local status    # whether it runs, and its nodes
   ```

   `meroctl local down` stops it; its state stays for the next `up`
   (`--fresh` starts empty).

5. **Sign in.** Sign up with a passkey kept in a file, which only a development
   cluster accepts:

   ```sh
   meroctl login --dev-passkey ./dev-passkey.json --name alice
   ```

   `login` signs up when the file does not exist yet, and signs in with it
   after. The sign-up also makes your personal organization.

6. **Create an instance and call it.** On a development cluster `--path`
   uploads a raw component; the instance goes in your personal organization:

   ```sh
   meroctl context create --name my-kv --path kv_store.wasm --alias my-kv
   meroctl call -c my-kv set --args '{"key": "hello", "value": "world"}'
   meroctl call -c my-kv get --args '{"key": "hello"}' --view
   ```

   The view answers the value with the log index it read and a receipt the
   answering node signed:

   ```json
   { "index": <n>, "result": "world", "receipt": { … } }
   ```

   Methods and arguments are the ABI's camelCase names (`getResult`,
   `updateIfExists`), and a `u64` travels as a decimal string:

   ```sh
   meroctl call -c my-kv len --view                       # result: "1"
   meroctl call -c my-kv getResult --args '{"key": "x"}' --view
   # refused: 422 APP_ERROR, code NotFound, fields { "key": "x" }
   meroctl context watch my-kv --limit 1                  # the Inserted event
   ```

7. **Pack it as a signed release.** A real cluster installs `.mpk` packages
   from its registry, never a raw component. `meroctl app pack` writes the
   manifest, signs it (here with the development key; see
   [Packaging & signing](/build/packaging-signing/) for your own) and packs
   the archive. A development cluster takes it as an upload too:

   ```sh
   meroctl app pack --wasm kv_store.wasm --package com.example.kv \
     --app-version 0.1.0 --out dist/com.example.kv-0.1.0.mpk
   meroctl app install --path dist/com.example.kv-0.1.0.mpk
   meroctl context create --name kv-pkg --package com.example.kv --alias kv-pkg
   ```

</Steps>

<Aside type="caution">
  A file passkey (`--dev-passkey`) and `--allow-mock` are for development
  clusters only: `meroctl login` refuses a file passkey on a node it does not
  trust as mock. On a real cluster you sign in with a passkey in the console
  and give `meroctl` an API key (`--api-key`).
</Aside>
